title: power-analysis result.json contract (merged GLS+PT-PX, SAIF flow)
description: Complete contract for asic/<module>/Verification/power-analysis/result.json. On status=pass, stage_specific requires saif_artifacts + compile_info + failures + ppa_actual + violations + power_by_corner (compile_info carries vcs_version only). On status=fail, stage_specific.{fail_reason, failure_kind} are required (if/then below); fail_reason is the one-line failure narrative. The heavy pass-shape is dropped on early-fail (external-reference / license / bootstrap paths). failure_kind classifies infra (the flow never ran) / tooling (it ran and its output is unusable) / ppa (power_mw exceeds target); the first two are declared by the caller through finalize's --fail-reason / --failure-kind, the third is the gate's. ppa_actual / violations / power_by_corner carry PT averaged power_mw + three components for PPA gating; on a PPA-gate fail (failure_kind=ppa) ppa_actual and violations are required (if/then below).

fix_owner.description: On status=fail: the rule that must act, named by this stage from what it read in the raw tool output. Deliberately NOT an enum — the derived input closure in rules.py is the only authority on which names are legal, and decide checks it there. Naming this stage itself (its in-stage remedy is exhausted) or naming nobody both mean a human decides.

ppa_gate_skipped.description: true when ppa_targets is empty (specification declared no power_mw target); status=pass is then vacuous, not a true PPA gate pass. Kept where the other write-only power fields went: it is not a record of what happened, it says WHICH proposition passed — 'power_mw <= target' with no target is a different claim, and a signoff reviewer endorsing it needs to see that.

failure_kind.description: Failure category on status=fail. infra = external reference / license / bootstrap missing, so GLS/PTPX never ran; tooling = they ran and their output is unusable; ppa = power_mw exceeds target. A declared fail (either of the first two) carries fail_reason and nothing structured: failures[] is the parser's to write, on the runs where it had reports to read.

failures.description: Tooling/data failures (NOT PPA gate failures — those go in violations[]).

category.description: What the parser itself detected, and only that: saif_dump = the SAIF came out empty; ptpx_data = a PT-PX report is absent, missing its Total, or fails the Total = internal+switching+leakage reconciliation. Nothing else writes this array, so the enum is exactly the set of conditions the parser has a branch for. The upstream-naming values it used to carry (netlist/sdf/tb_uvm/gls_runtime/plan) encoded WHOSE artifact was at fault, which fix_owner now states directly; tooling named this stage's own environment, which the parser cannot detect and never wrote.

violations.description: PPA violations when status=fail (power_mw exceeds target). Tooling failures go in failures[], not here.

saif_annotation_rate.description: Fraction of nets whose switching activity came from the SAIF, from switching_activity.rpt. Qualifies power_mw: the same number at 0.2 is mostly tool defaults, at 1.0 it is measured. null = not determinable from the report.
